title: Three Slaves
text: After that, I had a talk with the monster dealer and secured some wagons. A necessary item for putting on a circus, I say. We were forming a caravan, indeed. For the time being, Kuro-chan and the other Filolial-samas still in training would be the ones pulling it.
“The wagons can be pulled-nyaa?”
Once we regrouped near the monster dealer’s tent, I gave a little talk to Kuro-chan and the other Filolial-samas.
“Indeed. Under the monster dealer’s guidance, everyone shall put on a circus together, I say.”
“A circus?”
“Circus-nyaa!”
“Is a circus tasty?”
“A circus is a show where everyone travels together and has fun, indeed. And at each place we visit, Father will be buying and selling slaves.”
At that, Kuro-chan’s eyebrows drooped into a troubled shape.
“Ehh…… Kuro and the others have to help a Slave Trader with a Gift Unhappy?”

Kuro-chan seemed to be picking up on the general mood of the monster dealer’s tent. Come to think of it, the Filolial-samas were all creatures who loved fun above all else. It was only natural they’d feel uneasy about something as dark as the slave trade.
“I suppose it depends how you look at it. Kuro-chan, do you remember Rifana-chan and Raphtalia-chan, the ones we saved?”
“Yeah. They looked like they’d had a really hard time. Kuro warmed them up, didn’t she?”

“Well, in order to help the people from Rifana-chan and the others’ hometown, we need to buy slaves and gather them up to save them. And to do that, everyone’s going to pull the wagons, sing, dance, and put on a fun show for people everywhere. I want all of you to be that fun caravan troupe.”
A circus unlike any before, I say.
“Ohh! We’re doing a Dark Side Carnival-nyaa!?”
“Cannibal?”
“No, no, that’s a completely different word. Kuro-chan, are you even sure you know what you’re saying?”
“Carnival!”
“Carnival, indeed!”
“It’s a carnival!”

Upon hearing the word “carnival,” the Filolial-samas all started bouncing about happily. It seemed the idea of pulling wagons in order to sing, dance, and put on a fun circus had caught their interest.
“Got it-nyaa! Everyone’s gonna pull the wagons-nyaa!”
“Yaaay!”
“Sounds fun!”
“Yeah. It’ll be a lot of work, but we’ve got to sing and dance and do acrobatics and have fun doing it.”
“Yaaay!”
And so the Filolial-samas showed their enthusiasm all together.
“I’m glad Kuro-chan and the others are on board too.”
“The beginning of a delightful circus, indeed.”

“Right. Though we still need some time before we can officially open, since there’s a lot to work out for the program and all. We’re in the middle of getting location suggestions from the slave trader, and he says he’ll arrange the permits needed to hold the circus.”
So permits existed for such things too. What a bothersome world this was, what with its trade licenses and everything, I say.

“Also… the slave trader’s in the middle of picking out slaves to entrust to me, but do you want to check them too, Motoyasu-kun? It’s a bit much to suddenly designate slaves from Raphtalia-chan’s hometown, so it looks like I’ll have to manage a few through a separate channel.”
So there was a need to look after slaves other than those from the village. But there was no need to worry, I say.
“In the original world, Father originally looked after slaves who weren’t from the village too, indeed.”
Mole and Assistant were of that sort. And in later years, he purchased people as human resources regardless of village origin.
“Well then, should be fine. Let’s head back to the slave trader’s for now.”
And so we returned to the monster dealer’s tent.
“We’re back.”
Father addressed the monster dealer in a low, menacing voice.

“I’ve settled things with the Filolials. They looked reluctant about the slave trade at first, but I got their consent with some sweet talk. Told them it’d be a fun wagon trip, and they fell for it hook, line, and sinker.”
Kukuku… Father said, his tone dripping with theatrical villainy.
“Ohh, splendid. Your mastery over the human heart—er, Filolial heart—truly fills me with anticipation. Yes indeed.”
“So, how about your end? Picked out some decent-looking slaves?”
“I’ve had some fellow slave traders line up promising candidates as well, yes indeed. Since the Hero-sama has no experience handling slaves yet, I kept the selection small.”

It seemed others had been brought in chained from other merchants as well. One of them, along with two more brought out from the back of the monster dealer’s tent. One was… a rabbit-eared man with an arm bent at an odd angle.
“A male of the Rabbit species with a hereditary condition, yes indeed. Given how his arm is bent, there’s a decent chance he could draw some attention as a spectacle, yes indeed.”
“Hmm… a hereditary condition, is it.”

A spectacle slot, then. Meaning he’d be put on display for his abnormality without needing to be taught any particular skill. But this slave… I recognized him, indeed. He looked like the very slave Father had purchased back when he had Itsuki fill in for him while escaping the loop. If I recalled correctly, once Father diligently gave him some chiropractic treatment, that oddly bent arm became usable again, more or less normally. Of course, it wasn’t a complete cure just from that alone, but I remembered him becoming close to a healthy person, at least. It seemed the combination of leveling up and the Shield Hero’s blessing had helped him overcome the hereditary condition.
The Rabbit-species slave was staring at Father.
“Looks fast on his feet. Might be interesting to train him up and let the Filolials chase him down.”
“Ohh, splendid indeed! Having the Filolials hunt him down like they would an usapil would certainly make for quite a spectacle.”

Kukuku… Father laughed theatrically, and the monster dealer got all fired up in response. So Kuro-chan and the others would be chasing him. Everyone would surely enjoy a good game of tag—it would no doubt be a lively chase indeed. I’d flee on my motorcycle too, of course. Then Father turned his attention to the next slave. And this one… I recognized as well. A Lizardman whose gaze wandered—impossible to tell where he was looking. He had unusually strong human-like features for a Lizardman, but I recognized this one too. He was giving off killing intent. His features were so strongly human in places that his form ended up an awkward, half-finished mix.
“A mixed-breed Lizardman, yes indeed. His skeletal structure differs from a normal Lizardman’s—poor thing looks rather like a chimera, if I may say.”
“Hmm… another one for the spectacle slot, then.”
“Yes indeed. He’s also got a fair bit of strength, so he could be worked hard as a porter besides.”

“I see. There are probably things too heavy for the Filolials to carry anyway, so that’s not bad. Might be good to parade a guy like this around too. The Siltvelt folks would probably hate it, wouldn’t they? Bunch of purity-obsessed types, from what I hear.”
“I take my hat off to the Shield Hero-sama’s wisdom, yes indeed.”
For just a moment, the Lizardman’s eyes returned to normal. It seemed he was putting on that deranged expression on purpose, as if trying to avoid being purchased.
“And last but not least…”
“Grrrrrrr……”
And last was the wolf-man I’d been shown earlier.
“This one’s our headliner—a high-level slave who fought in the Coliseum, now crippled beyond recovery, yes indeed.”
Deep scars ran along his arms and legs. It was doubtful whether healing magic or medicine could even fix that at this point—the treatment costs alone would probably exceed his worth.
“Having a human whip a powerful species to show who’s superior—that’s an essential part of the show, yes indeed.”
The monster dealer flared up the brand with a sharp gesture.
“Yipe-yipe! Grrrrooowl! Gaaah!”
Writhing in pain, the wolf-man leapt at Father in a fit of rage.
Without a word, Father caught the lunging wolf-man’s nose in a firm grip.
“Yip!? Grrrrr……”
The wolf-man went cross-eyed the instant his nose was seized. Perhaps the brand’s pain caught up to him then, because he collapsed right there, writhing in agony.
“Quite the lively one, this slave.”
“Precisely why the show will be such a hit, yes indeed.”
“I see—so it’s making money off dog training, essentially.”

Kukuku… Father chuckled along in agreement with the monster dealer’s words. Then he casually turned to face me, wearing an expression that seemed to ask what we should do. Conveniently at an angle the monster dealer couldn’t see. Time for a hushed conversation, indeed.
